summary: Episode 3 became evergreen for the same reason episode 4 did: the guest and the host later became a real couple. The top comment is simply 'admit it, you came back because of the Meen and Dream news', and a large share of the thread is people confessing exactly that, timestamping near-misses as evidence — one notes the guest was about to reach for her hand before another host interrupted. The second-largest cluster is defensive: Dream is being judged by the guest's fanbase, and commenters push back by listing her education, family standing and clean record, ending with 'and finally, he loves her'. So the romance imports a hostile audience alongside the loyal one. A steady cluster is guest requests, with Te Tawan, Lee Thanat and Fey named repeatedly and upvote calls attached. Several people ask for the guest to return specifically as Dream's boyfriend to compare his behaviour before and after.

audience_signals: Two of this series' five most-viewed episodes became evergreen because a host later dated the guest — the format manufactures real romances, and those are the channel's strongest retention engine

The same mechanic imports hostility: the guest's fanbase questions the host's worthiness, and the channel's own audience has to defend her, so romance news is a reputational cost as well as a reach gain
Viewers rewatch at frame level, timestamping near-touches — depth of attention that makes editing choices consequential years later
The guest-request list here overlaps with episode 4's, so the same names have been asked for repeatedly across years without being booked
There is explicit demand for a 'then and now' return episode with the same guest in his new status, which is a low-cost, high-interest sequel
